description:
DEBT CREATED BY fz-5xp.1, filed as its price rather than left to drift.

fz-5xp.1 filled the entry-dispatch hole by writing a THIRD reading of the same
question. Before it there were two implementations and one hole; after it there
are three implementations. That is the shape fz-5xp.18 had just finished
proving expensive, and this ticket exists so the count goes back down.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY FOLDABLE -- verified, because "three into one" is not available:

  EMITTERS (two, foldable):
    native_codegen/receive.rs:1083   emit_bitstring_test
      Emits Cranelift directly, into a standalone C-ABI leaf function the
      scheduler calls: extern "C" fn(msg_ref, pinned, out) -> u32, returning a
      1-based clause index and writing bound values into a caller buffer
      (runtime/src/park.rs MatcherFn). Carries PatternDispatchPlan<RuntimeTypePredicate>.
    compiler2/jobs/native.rs         lower_bitstring_region
      Emits fz IR -- ctx.emit_let / Term::If / block parameters -- as inline
      control flow inside an ordinary compiled function. Carries
      PatternDispatchPlan<Ty>.
    Same Region enum, same semantics, different emission target, different type
    handle. One of these should be expressed in terms of the other, or both in
    terms of a shared description of a region test.

  EXECUTOR (one, NOT code-shareable):
    ir_interp/dispatch_exec.rs:591   dispatch_read_bitstring
      Walks runtime values rather than emitting instructions. An interpreter and
      a backend cannot share this body. What keeps it honest is the parity gate,
      not a shared function.

So the target is ONE EMITTER + ONE EXECUTOR + A GATE, not one implementation.

SCOPE NOTE: this is bigger than bitstrings. Region::Type, Region::Equal,
Region::List, Region::TupleArity, Region::MapKeyPresent and Region::Guard are
ALL implemented in both emitters today. Bitstring is simply the one where the
duplication became visible, because entry dispatch never got its copy. Folding
only the bitstring arm would be the least valuable version of this ticket.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: the divergence is not hypothetical. fz-5xp.18
found `2 >= 1.0` answering false on one door and true on another for exactly
this reason, and a third comparison implementation in guards that was wrong on
BOTH doors. Every region kind duplicated across the two emitters is a pair that
can drift the same way, and only a fixture that exercises the region on every
door will notice.

GATE: fixtures2/behavior/bitstring_clause_dispatch.fz already covers the
bitstring region on all three doors against an Elixir twin. A fold should keep
it green without being re-blessed.

Related: fz-5xp.21 audits which semantic questions are answered more than once;
this is the dispatch-layer instance of that audit.

comments.text:
MEASURED, and it is bigger than the ticket title says. All TEN region kinds are
implemented in all THREE files -- the sets are identical:

  Bitstring  Cons  Empty  Equal  Guard  List  MapKeyPresent  MapKind  TupleArity  Type

  native_codegen/receive.rs   all 10   (Cranelift, C-ABI leaf matcher fn)
  compiler2/jobs/native.rs    all 10   (fz IR, inline control flow)
  ir_interp/dispatch_exec.rs  all 10   (executes runtime values)

That is 30 implementations of 10 questions. It was never a bitstring problem.
Bitstring is simply the ONLY place the duplication was visible, because entry
dispatch had a hole there and refused to lower; the other nine have had three
readings each all along, silently.

This is the same class fz-5xp.18 proved drifts. Comparison had three readings
and two of them were wrong in different ways: `2 >= 1.0` answered false on the
JIT and true on interp, and guards answered a mixed comparison wrongly on BOTH
doors. Nothing structural stops any of these thirty from drifting the same way;
what stopped it so far is that most regions are exercised by fixtures that
happen to run on every door.

So the ticket is: ONE EMITTER + ONE EXECUTOR + A GATE, across the whole Region
enum -- not a bitstring fix. Sequencing suggestion: pick a region kind whose
three readings are simplest (Empty or TupleArity), fold those first to establish
the seam, then move the rest behind it.

The executor cannot join the fold -- an interpreter walking values and a backend
emitting instructions cannot share a body -- so the gate is what keeps it
honest. Check what that gate currently is: a region only stays honest if some
fixture exercises it on all three doors, and mixed int/float comparison survived
for as long as it did because no fixture compared an integer to a float.

title: Fold the two native dispatch region emitters into one
